records.source: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν ὄχλον ἐπικεῖσθαι αὐτῷ καὶ ἀκούειν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἑστὼς παρὰ τὴν λίμνην Γεννησαρὲτ, καὶ εἶδεν δύο πλοῖα ἑστῶτα παρὰ τὴν λίμνην, οἱ δὲ ἁλιεῖς ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀποβάντες ἔπλυνον τὰ δίκτυα.
records.gloss: It came to pass then in the the crowd to press upon him and to hear the word of the God, and he was standing beside the lake Gennesaret, \v 2 and he saw two boats standing beside the lake; the and fishermen from them having gone out were washing the nets.
pieces: Once, as Jesus stood beside the lake of Gennesaret, the crowd was pushing in around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to hear the word of God.
He noticed two boats drawn up at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had climbed out of them and were washing their nets.

L.1: And it happened, while the crowd was pressing on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and hearing the word of God, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret,
L.2: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw two boats standing beside the lake; but the fishermen had gone out of them and were washing the nets.

R.1: One day Jesus was standing on the shore of Lake Gennesaret. A crowd of people was pushing close to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to listen to God's message.
R.2: Jesus saw two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had left their boats and were washing their nets.

decisions.choice: the lake of Gennesaret: the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Gennesaret was the fertile plain on the north-west shore of the lake, and the lake was also called by its name. Mark and Matthew call it the Sea of Galilee (Mark 1:16); John calls it the Sea of Tiberias (John 21:1). Luke always calls it a lake (8:22-23).

decisions.choice: the word of God: Jesus's teaching, which is God's message
decisions.reason: Luke uses the phrase for the message Jesus proclaims (8:11, 21) and later for the message the apostles preach (Acts 4:31; 6:2).

decisions.choice: washing the nets: cleaning and mending them after a night's work
decisions.reason: Fishermen on the lake worked with nets at night (5:5) and cleaned them in the morning, so that weed and mud would not rot them.

decisions.choice: Jesus (B, R); he (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section of the story.

decisions.choice: God's message
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the word" means here.

records.heading: The great catch of fish and the call of Simon

records.source: ἐμβὰς δὲ εἰς ἓν τῶν πλοίων, ὃ ἦν Σίμωνος, ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἐπαναγαγεῖν ὀλίγον, καθίσας δὲ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου ἐδίδασκεν τοὺς ὄχλους.
records.gloss: Having entered then into one of the boats, which was of Simon, he asked him from the land to put out a little; having sat down then out of the boat he was teaching the crowds.
pieces: He got into one of the boats, the one that belonged to Simon, and asked him to push off a short way from the shore. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down and taught the crowds from the boat.

L.3: And getting into one of the boats, which was Simon's, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked him to put out a little from the land; and sitting down, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching the crowds from the boat.

R.3: Jesus got into one of the boats. It belonged to Simon. Jesus asked Simon to push the boat out a little way from the shore. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down in the boat and taught the people.

decisions.choice: having sat down: Jewish teachers usually sat to teach
decisions.reason: Jesus sat down to teach in the synagogue at Nazareth (4:20), as teachers did. From the boat he could see the whole crowd on the shore.

decisions.choice: Simon: the man whose mother-in-law Jesus has already healed
decisions.reason: Jesus has been in Simon's house in Capernaum (4:38-39). Luke introduces him by his own name; Jesus will name him Peter (6:14).

records.source: ὡς δὲ ἐπαύσατο λαλῶν, εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα· Ἐπανάγαγε εἰς τὸ βάθος καὶ χαλάσατε τὰ δίκτυα ὑμῶν εἰς ἄγραν.
records.gloss: When then he stopped speaking, he said to the Simon, Put out into the deep and let down the nets of you for a catch.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had finished speaking, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told Simon, "Take the boat out where the water is deep, and lower your nets to catch fish."

L.4: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stopped speaking, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to Simon, "Put out into the deep [water], and let down your nets for a catch."

R.4: When Jesus finished teaching, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to Simon, "Take the boat out into deep water. Then put your nets down into the water to catch some fish."

decisions.choice: put out (to Simon alone), let down your nets (to Simon and his crew)
decisions.reason: The first verb is singular and the second is plural. Simon steers the boat; the whole crew handles the nets.

decisions.choice: deep water by day: against the fishermen's experience
alternatives: the usual time and place to fish
decisions.reason: Fishermen on the lake worked through the night (5:5). Simon's answer shows that he did not expect a catch.

decisions.choice: to catch fish
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what is caught.

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν· Ἐπιστάτα, δι’ ὅλης νυκτὸς κοπιάσαντες οὐδὲν ἐλάβομεν, ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ ῥήματί σου χαλάσω τὰ δίκτυα.
records.gloss: And answering Simon said, Master, through whole night having toiled nothing we took; at but the word of you I will let down the nets.
pieces: Simon replied, "Master, we worked hard the whole night through and caught nothing. But on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word I will lower the nets."

L.5: And Simon answered and said, "Master, we toiled through [the] whole night and took nothing, but at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word I will let down the nets."

R.5: Simon answered, "Master, we worked hard all night, and we did not catch a thing. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} told me to do it, so I will put the nets down."

decisions.choice: Master: one who has authority and gives orders
decisions.reason: Only Luke uses this word in the New Testament, and always for Jesus, mostly on the lips of his disciples (8:24, 45; 9:33). It was used of an overseer or commander. Simon will soon call Jesus "Lord" (5:8).

decisions.choice: your word: your command
decisions.reason: The noun means a spoken word. Simon obeys an order that goes against his experience.

decisions.choice: toiled: worked to the point of weariness
decisions.reason: The verb means hard, tiring work.

decisions.choice: you told me to do it, so I will put the nets down
alternatives: at your word I will let down the nets
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that Simon acts because Jesus told him to.

records.source: καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσαντες συνέκλεισαν πλῆθος ἰχθύων πολύ, διερρήσσετο δὲ τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And this having done they enclosed a multitude of fish great, were being torn and the nets of them.
pieces: So they did this, and they closed their nets around a great mass of fish. Their nets were starting to tear.

L.6: And when they had done this, they enclosed a great number of fish, and their nets were beginning to tear.

R.6: They did what Jesus said. They caught so many fish that the nets started tearing apart.

decisions.choice: were breaking: the nets began to tear
alternatives: the nets broke and the fish were lost
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes what was starting to happen. The catch was saved (5:7, 9).

decisions.choice: what Jesus said
decisions.reason: Readable says what they had done.

records.source: καὶ κατένευσαν τοῖς μετόχοις ἐν τῷ ἑτέρῳ πλοίῳ τοῦ ἐλθόντας συλλαβέσθαι αὐτοῖς· καὶ ἦλθον, καὶ ἔπλησαν ἀμφότερα τὰ πλοῖα ὥστε βυθίζεσθαι αὐτά.
records.gloss: And they signaled to the partners in the other boat, the having come to help them; and they came, and filled both the boats so that were sinking them.
pieces: They waved to their partners in the other boat to come over and lend a hand. The partners came, and together they loaded both boats with fish until the boats were starting to go under.

L.7: And they signaled to [their] partners in the other boat to come [and] help them; and they came and filled both boats, so that they were beginning to sink.

R.7: So they waved to the men in the other boat, who worked with them, to come and help. The men came. They put so many fish into both boats that the boats were about to sink.

decisions.choice: partners: fellow fishermen who worked with Simon
decisions.reason: Luke names them in 5:10: James and John, Zebedee's sons, who were partners with Simon.

decisions.choice: were sinking: were beginning to sink
decisions.reason: The verb describes what was about to happen; the boats reached land (5:11).

decisions.choice: the men in the other boat, who worked with them
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word.

records.source: ἰδὼν δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος προσέπεσεν τοῖς γόνασιν Ἰησοῦ λέγων· Ἔξελθε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτωλός εἰμι, κύριε·
records.gloss: Having seen and Simon Peter fell at the knees of Jesus saying, Depart from me, for a man sinful I am, Lord.
pieces: When Simon Peter saw this, he threw himself down at Jesus's knees and said, "Lord, leave me! I am a man full of sin."

L.8: And when Simon Peter saw [it], he fell down at the knees of Jesus, saying, "Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord."

R.8: When Simon Peter saw this, he knelt down in front of Jesus. He said, "Lord, go away from me! I am a sinner, and I am not fit to be near {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

decisions.choice: Peter: the name Jesus gives Simon
decisions.reason: Luke tells in 6:14 that Jesus named Simon "Peter", which means rock. Here, at the moment Simon is called, Luke uses both names.

decisions.choice: Lord: more than a polite title here
decisions.reason: The same word can be a polite "sir". Simon called Jesus "Master" (5:5); now, on his knees and confessing his sin, he uses the word Luke uses for God and for Jesus (2:11).

decisions.choice: depart from me, for I am a sinful man: the fear of a sinful person before God's holiness
alternatives: embarrassment at his failure as a fisherman
decisions.reason: When Isaiah saw the Lord, he cried out that he was lost, a man of unclean lips (Isaiah 6:5). Simon sees God's power at work in Jesus and feels unworthy to be near him.

decisions.choice: I am not fit to be near you
decisions.reason: Readable spells out why Simon asks Jesus to leave, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: θάμβος γὰρ περιέσχεν αὐτὸν καὶ πάντας τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἄγρᾳ τῶν ἰχθύων ὧν συνέλαβον, ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου, οἳ ἦσαν κοινωνοὶ τῷ Σίμωνι.
records.gloss: Amazement for seized him and all the [ones] with him at the catch of the fish which they took, \v 10 likewise and also James and John sons of Zebedee, who were partners with the Simon.
pieces: He said this because the haul of fish they had brought in had left him stunned, and all who were with him as well.
Zebedee's sons, James and John, Simon's partners, were stunned in the same way.

L.9: For amazement had seized him and all those with him at the catch of fish that they had taken,
L.10: and likewise also James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon.

R.9: Simon and all the men with him were amazed at how many fish they had caught.
R.10: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, were amazed too. They were Simon's partners in the fishing business.

decisions.choice: for: this explains Simon's words in 5:8
decisions.reason: Simon spoke as he did because the catch had overwhelmed him.

decisions.choice: amazement: astonishment mixed with fear
decisions.reason: The word is used of people faced with a power they cannot explain (4:36; Acts 3:10).

decisions.choice: partners: sharers in a business
decisions.reason: The word means people who share something, here a fishing business.

decisions.choice: He said this because
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the connection with 5:8 plain.

decisions.choice: partners in the fishing business
decisions.reason: Readable says what they were partners in.

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ φοβοῦ· ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀνθρώπους ἔσῃ ζωγρῶν.
records.gloss: And said to the Simon the Jesus, Not fear; from the now people you will be catching alive.
pieces: "Do not be afraid," Jesus told Simon. "From now on you will be catching {{gender:people|men}}."

L.10: And Jesus said to Simon, "Do not be afraid; from now on you will be catching {{gender:people|men}} alive."

R.10: "Do not be afraid," Jesus said to Simon. "From now on you will catch {{gender:people|men}} instead of fish."

decisions.choice: catching alive: taking people alive, to save them
decisions.reason: The verb means to take alive, as soldiers took prisoners alive. Fish that are caught die; the people Simon catches will live. Simon's work will be to gather people for God.

decisions.choice: people: human beings, men and women
decisions.reason: The noun is the general word for human beings.

decisions.choice: you will be catching: an ongoing work
decisions.reason: "Will be" with the participle describes a lasting task from now on.

decisions.choice: do not be afraid: Simon need not fear being near Jesus
alternatives: do not fear the storm or the sea
decisions.reason: Jesus answers Simon's fear in 5:8, as angels answered Zechariah and Mary (1:13, 30).

decisions.choice: instead of fish
decisions.reason: Readable makes the comparison with Simon's work plain. It does not try to bring out "alive", which the meaning decision explains.

records.source: καὶ καταγαγόντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἀφέντες πάντα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: And having brought the boats onto the land, having left all they followed him.
pieces: Once the boats were on land, they walked away from everything and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.11: And when they had brought the boats to land, they left everything and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.11: They brought their boats to the shore. Then they left everything behind and followed Jesus.

decisions.choice: followed: went with him as his disciples
alternatives: walked behind him for a time
decisions.reason: To follow Jesus is to become his disciple and share his life (5:27-28; 9:23).

decisions.choice: everything: their boats, their trade, and even the great catch
decisions.reason: They leave behind the very catch they had just made. Levi will do the same (5:28; 18:28).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

records.source: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν μιᾷ τῶν πόλεων καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ πλήρης λέπρας· καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἐδεήθη αὐτοῦ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.
records.gloss: And it came to pass in the being him in one of the cities and look a man full of leprosy; having seen and the Jesus, having fallen on face he begged him saying, Lord, if you are willing, you are able me to cleanse.
pieces: In one of the towns where Jesus was, there was a man covered all over with leprosy. Seeing Jesus, he fell face down and pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can make me clean, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} choose to."

L.12: And it happened, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in one of the towns, that look, [there was] a man full of leprosy; and when he saw Jesus, he fell on [his] face and begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Lord, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are willing, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able to make me clean."

R.12: Jesus was in one of the towns. A man there had a terrible skin disease all over his body. When the man saw Jesus, he bowed down with his face to the ground. He begged Jesus, "Lord, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want to, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can heal me and make me clean."

decisions.choice: leprosy: a serious skin disease that made a person unclean under the law
alternatives: only the disease now called leprosy (Hansen's disease)
decisions.reason: The law of Moses gives the word to several kinds of skin disease, and even to mold in clothing and houses (Leviticus 13-14). A priest examined the skin and declared the person clean or unclean. Someone with the disease had to tear his clothes, cry "Unclean!" and live outside the camp, apart from others (Leviticus 13:45-46), and could not take part in worship.

decisions.choice: full of leprosy: the disease covered his body
decisions.reason: "Full of" means the disease had spread over much of his body. Luke, the doctor (Colossians 4:14), alone notes it.

decisions.choice: make clean: heal, so that he can be declared clean
decisions.reason: The law speaks of "cleansing" from this disease (Leviticus 14:2). A priest could declare a person clean once the disease had gone, but could not make it go. The man asks Jesus to do what the law could not.

decisions.choice: if you are willing, you can: the man does not doubt Jesus's power, only whether he wants to use it for him
decisions.reason: The question is not whether Jesus can, but whether he will.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: a terrible skin disease; heal me and make me clean
decisions.reason: Readable describes the disease instead of naming it, because "leprosy" now means one particular disease. It also says that being clean meant being healed.

decisions.choice: you can make me clean, if you choose to
alternatives: if you are willing, you can make me clean
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the man's confidence first and his request second.

records.heading: Jesus makes a man with leprosy clean

records.source: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἥψατο αὐτοῦ εἰπών· Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι· καὶ εὐθέως ἡ λέπρα ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And having stretched out the hand he touched him saying, I am willing, be cleansed; and immediately the leprosy departed from him.
pieces: He stretched out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and laid it on the man. "I do want to," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "Be made clean." The leprosy left him that very moment.

L.13: And stretching out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched him, saying, "I am willing; be cleansed." And immediately the leprosy departed from him.

R.13: Jesus put out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and touched the man. "I do want to," Jesus said. "Be healed and clean!" Right away the man's skin disease was gone.

decisions.choice: he touched him: touching an unclean person made a person unclean
alternatives: a touch with no special meaning
decisions.reason: The law treated contact with an unclean person as making a person unclean (Leviticus 5:3). Jesus is not made unclean; instead the man is made clean.

decisions.choice: be cleansed: a command that takes effect at once
decisions.reason: The passive command answers the man's request word for word, and Luke says the disease left at once.

decisions.choice: I am willing: the answer to "if you are willing"
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up the man's own verb from 5:12.

decisions.choice: the man (B, R); him (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear whom Jesus touched.

records.source: καὶ αὐτὸς παρήγγειλεν αὐτῷ μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν, ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν δεῖξον σεαυτὸν τῷ ἱερεῖ, καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου καθὼς προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: And he ordered him no one to tell, but having gone show yourself to the priest and offer for the cleansing of you as commanded Moses, for a testimony to them.
pieces: Jesus gave him strict orders not to tell anyone. "Instead," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "go and let the priest examine you. Then bring the offering Moses ordered for your cleansing, as evidence to them."

L.14: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ordered him to tell no one, "But go, show yourself to the priest, and make an offering for your cleansing, as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."

R.14: Jesus told him, "Do not tell anyone about this. Instead, go to the priest and let him look at your skin. Then give the offering that Moses commanded for people who have been made clean. This will show everyone that you are healed."

decisions.choice: show yourself to the priest and offer: the steps the law of Moses set out for a person cleansed of the disease
alternatives: a new rule given by Jesus
decisions.reason: Leviticus 14:1-32 tells how a priest examined the person outside the camp, and how, after washing and offerings of birds and lambs (or doves for the poor), the person was declared clean and could return to the community and its worship.

decisions.choice: the order begins as reported speech and turns into Jesus's own words
decisions.reason: Luke moves from "he ordered him to tell no one" straight into the words Jesus spoke, "but go, show yourself". He does the same in Acts 1:4.

decisions.choice: as a testimony to them: as evidence to the priests and the people that the man is clean
decisions.reason: The priest's declaration would let everyone know the man was clean again, and so would show what God had done. Some take "them" as the priests and the testimony as a challenge to them.

decisions.choice: the order to tell no one also as Jesus's own words (R); reported, then quoted (L, B)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the shift into direct speech; Readable puts all of the order in Jesus's words, which is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: This will show everyone that you are healed
decisions.reason: Readable gives the more likely sense, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: διήρχετο δὲ μᾶλλον ὁ λόγος περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ συνήρχοντο ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀκούειν καὶ θεραπεύεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀσθενειῶν αὐτῶν·
records.gloss: Was spreading and still more the word about him, and were coming together crowds many to hear and to be healed from the sicknesses of them;
pieces: But word about Jesus went out farther than ever. Large crowds kept gathering to listen and to be healed of their illnesses.

L.15: But the word about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was spreading still more, and many crowds were coming together to hear and to be healed of their sicknesses.

R.15: But the news about Jesus kept spreading even more. Big crowds came to hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} teach, and to have {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} heal their sicknesses.

decisions.choice: the word about him: the report, the news
decisions.reason: The noun means a spoken account; here what people were saying about Jesus (7:17).

decisions.choice: but still more: in spite of the order to tell no one, the news spread even more
decisions.reason: Luke does not say who spread it; he says the order did not stop it.

decisions.choice: Jesus (B, R); him (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: to hear him teach, and to have him heal
alternatives: to hear and to be healed
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they came to hear and who healed them.

records.source: αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν ὑποχωρῶν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις καὶ προσευχόμενος.
records.gloss: He himself but was withdrawing in the wilderness [places] and praying.
pieces: Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept slipping away to places in the wilderness to pray.

L.16: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} would withdraw into the wilderness [places] and pray.

R.16: But Jesus would often go away to places where no one lived, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could pray.

decisions.choice: was withdrawing and praying: his habit
decisions.reason: "Was" with the participles describes something Jesus did again and again. Prayer marks the turning points of Jesus's life in Luke (3:21; 6:12; 9:18).

decisions.choice: the wilderness places: lonely places away from towns
decisions.reason: The word is plural: deserted places, as in 4:42.

decisions.choice: he himself, but: in contrast to the crowds seeking him
decisions.reason: Luke sets Jesus's withdrawal against the crowds who came to him (5:15).

decisions.choice: kept slipping away (B); would often go away (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the habit, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διδάσκων, καὶ ἦσαν καθήμενοι Φαρισαῖοι καὶ νομοδιδάσκαλοι οἳ ἦσαν ἐληλυθότες ἐκ πάσης κώμης τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ· καὶ δύναμις κυρίου ἦν εἰς τὸ ἰᾶσθαι αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And it came to pass on one of the days and he was teaching, and were sitting Pharisees and teachers of the law who were having come out of every village of the Galilee and Judea and Jerusalem; and power of Lord was for the to heal him.
pieces: On one of those days, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching, some Pharisees and teachers of the law were seated there. They had come from all the villages of Galilee, from Judea, and from Jerusalem. The power of the Lord was present for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to heal.

L.17: And it happened on one of the days that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching, and Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting [there], who had come out of every village of Galilee and Judea and [from] Jerusalem; and [the] power of [the] Lord was [there] for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to heal.

R.17: One day Jesus was teaching. Some Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. They had come from every town in Galilee and Judea, and from Jerusalem. The Lord God was giving Jesus power to heal people.

decisions.choice: Pharisees: a movement of Jews devoted to keeping the law of Moses exactly
decisions.reason: The Pharisees studied the law closely and kept the traditions handed down by earlier teachers on how to obey it, especially about the Sabbath, tithing, fasting and ritual cleanness (Galatians 1:14; Acts 26:5). Paul had been one (Philippians 3:5). Many people respected them. This is their first appearance in Luke.

decisions.choice: teachers of the law: experts who taught and explained the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The word is used of Gamaliel, a Pharisee honored by all the people (Acts 5:34). Luke also calls these experts "scribes" (5:21).

decisions.choice: him: the power of the Lord was there for Jesus to heal, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: them: for him to heal them, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts read "him", as the subject of the healing. Many later manuscripts read "them", the sick he healed. The sense is close. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the power of the Lord: God's power
decisions.reason: "Lord" here is God, as often in Luke 1-2 (1:66; 2:9). Jesus heals by the power of the Spirit (4:14, 18).

decisions.choice: teachers of the law
decisions.reason: This word means teachers of the law, so every level says so. Luke's other word for these experts is rendered "scribes" (L, B) in 5:21.

decisions.choice: The Lord God was giving Jesus power to heal people
alternatives: the power of the Lord was there for him to heal
decisions.reason: Readable says whose power it was and whom Jesus healed.

records.heading: Authority on earth to forgive sins

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες φέροντες ἐπὶ κλίνης ἄνθρωπον ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος, καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν εἰσενεγκεῖν καὶ θεῖναι ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And look men carrying on a bed a man who was paralyzed, and they were seeking him to bring in and to place before him.
pieces: Just then some men arrived with a paralyzed man lying on a bed. They wanted to carry him in and lay him in front of Jesus.

L.18: And look, men [were] carrying on a bed a man who was paralyzed, and they were trying to bring him in and to lay [him] before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.18: Some men brought a man who could not move his body. They carried him on a mat. They wanted to take him into the house and put him down in front of Jesus.

decisions.choice: a bed: a light pallet or mat that could be carried
decisions.reason: The word is a general word for a bed. Luke calls it a little bed in 5:19 and 24: something light enough for men to carry.

decisions.choice: paralyzed: unable to move his limbs
decisions.reason: The man had to be carried; he could not walk (5:23-25).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: into the house
decisions.reason: Readable says where they wanted to bring him; the roof in 5:19 shows it was a house.

decisions.choice: a mat
decisions.reason: Readable uses the word for something light that could be carried.

records.source: καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ποίας εἰσενέγκωσιν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀναβάντες ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα διὰ τῶν κεράμων καθῆκαν αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ κλινιδίῳ εἰς τὸ μέσον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: And not having found by what [way] they might bring in him because of the crowd, having gone up on the roof through the tiles they let down him with the little bed into the middle in front of the Jesus.
pieces: The crowd left them no way of getting him in. So they climbed up on the roof, took away some of the tiles, and let him down on his bed into the middle of everyone, in front of Jesus.

L.19: And not finding by what [way] they might bring him in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and let him down through the tiles with [his] little bed into the middle, in front of Jesus.

R.19: But there were too many people, and the men could not get him through the crowd. So they went up onto the flat roof of the house. They removed some of the tiles and made a hole. Then they let the man down on his mat into the middle of the people, right in front of Jesus.

decisions.choice: the roof, the tiles: a flat roof that could be opened
decisions.reason: Houses in the land of Israel had flat roofs, often reached by an outside stair, where people could walk (Deuteronomy 22:8; Acts 10:9). Mark says the men dug through the roof (Mark 2:4); Luke speaks of tiles.

decisions.choice: the little bed: the same pallet as in 5:18
decisions.reason: Luke uses a smaller form of the word for the same light bed.

decisions.choice: took away (B) or removed (R) some of the tiles
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how they made a way through.

decisions.choice: the flat roof of the house
decisions.reason: Readable explains how men could climb onto a roof.

records.source: καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἄνθρωπε, ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου.
records.gloss: And having seen the faith of them he said, Man, have been forgiven to you the sins of you.
pieces: Jesus saw their faith and said, "My friend, your sins stand forgiven."

L.20: And seeing their faith, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Man, your sins have been forgiven you."

R.20: Jesus saw that they had faith. He said to the man, "My friend, God has forgiven your sins."

decisions.choice: their faith: the trust of the men who brought him, and probably of the man himself, shown in what they did
alternatives: the faith of the paralyzed man alone
decisions.reason: Their effort to reach Jesus showed that they trusted him to help. In Luke faith is often seen in action (7:9, 50; 8:48).

decisions.choice: have been forgiven: forgiven, and that stands; God is the one who forgives
decisions.reason: The perfect tense describes a forgiveness that holds. The passive leaves God as the one who forgives, which is why the scribes object (5:21).

decisions.choice: Man: a plain, kind way to address someone
decisions.reason: Calling someone "man" was neither rude nor cold (12:14; 22:58).

decisions.choice: My friend
decisions.reason: In modern English "Man" as an address sounds rough. Balanced and Readable give the friendly tone.

decisions.choice: God has forgiven
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who forgives, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: καὶ ἤρξαντο διαλογίζεσθαι οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες· Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὃς λαλεῖ βλασφημίας;
records.gloss: And began to reason the scribes and the Pharisees saying, Who is this who speaks blasphemies?
pieces: The scribes and Pharisees started to debate among themselves: "Who is this man, speaking blasphemy like this?

L.21: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, "Who is this who speaks blasphemies?

R.21: The teachers of the law and the Pharisees began to ask themselves, "Who is this man? His words are an insult to God!

decisions.choice: scribes: experts in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The word first meant a writer or clerk. In the Gospels it means the experts who copied, studied and taught the law, the same people Luke has just called teachers of the law (5:17).

decisions.choice: blasphemies: words that insult God
decisions.reason: To speak blasphemy was to dishonor God, and the law punished it severely (Leviticus 24:16). They think Jesus has claimed something that belongs to God alone.

decisions.choice: reason: think it over and debate, here in their hearts
decisions.reason: The verb is used of thinking and arguing among people or within oneself. Jesus asks why they reason "in your hearts" (5:22).

decisions.choice: teachers of the law (R); scribes (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable avoids the word "scribes", which today suggests copying, and calls them what they were.

decisions.choice: His words are an insult to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "blasphemy".

records.source: τίς δύναται ἁμαρτίας ἀφεῖναι εἰ μὴ μόνος ὁ θεός;
records.gloss: Who is able sins to forgive except alone the God?
pieces: Who has the power to forgive sins? Only God!"

L.21: Who is able to forgive sins except God alone?"

decisions.choice: who can forgive sins but God alone: the teaching of the Scriptures
alternatives: a rule of their own making
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures it is God who blots out sins (Isaiah 43:25) and forgives wrongdoing (Exodus 34:6-7; Psalm 103:3). They are right that only God forgives; the question is who Jesus is (5:24).

decisions.choice: a statement
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one"; Readable states it.

records.source: ἐπιγνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;
records.gloss: Having known and the Jesus the reasonings of them, answering he said to them, Why are you reasoning in the hearts of you?
pieces: Jesus was aware of what was going through their minds, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} replied, "Why do you debate this in your hearts?

L.22: But Jesus, knowing their reasonings, answered and said to them, "Why are you reasoning in your hearts?

R.22: Jesus knew what they were thinking. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Why are you having such thoughts?

decisions.choice: knowing: knowing fully, seeing into their thoughts
decisions.reason: Luke shows Jesus knowing what people think (6:8; 9:47), something people expected of a prophet (7:39).

decisions.choice: in your hearts: in your minds
decisions.reason: In the Bible the heart is where a person thinks and decides.

decisions.choice: answering: Jesus answers what they had not said aloud
decisions.reason: Luke uses "answered" for Jesus replying to their thoughts.

decisions.choice: in your hearts (B); not rendered (R)
decisions.reason: Readable leaves out the picture, which in modern English suggests feelings.

records.source: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν· Ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου, ἢ εἰπεῖν· Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει;
records.gloss: Which is easier, to say, Have been forgiven to you the sins of you, or to say, Rise and walk?
pieces: Which is easier to say: 'Your sins stand forgiven,' or 'Get up and walk'?

L.23: Which is easier, to say, 'Your sins have been forgiven you,' or to say, 'Rise and walk'?

R.23: Is it easier to say to this man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?

decisions.choice: which is easier to say: the question compares saying the two things
decisions.reason: Anyone can say "your sins are forgiven", since no one can see whether it happened. Saying "get up and walk" is tested at once. Jesus will do the second to show that the first is true (5:24).

decisions.choice: to this man
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the words are spoken.

records.source: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας εἶπεν τῷ παραλελυμένῳ· Σοὶ λέγω, ἔγειρε καὶ ἄρας τὸ κλινίδιόν σου πορεύου εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.
records.gloss: That but you may know that the Son of the Man authority has on the earth to forgive sins, he said to the [one] paralyzed, To you I say, rise and having taken up the little bed of you go to the house of you.
pieces: But to show you that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the paralyzed man, "I tell you, stand up, take your bed, and go off to your house."

L.24: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the paralyzed man, "I say to you, rise, and take up your little bed and go to your house."

R.24: But I will prove to you that the Son of Man has the right to forgive sins here on earth." Then Jesus said to the man who could not move, "I tell you, get up! Pick up your mat and go home."

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's name for himself, recalling Daniel 7:13-14
alternatives: a son of man: simply a human being
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "son of man" can mean simply a human being (Psalm 8:5; Ezekiel 2:1). In Daniel 7:13-14 one like a son of man receives authority and everlasting rule from God. In the Gospels Jesus uses the title of himself. This is its first use in Luke.

decisions.choice: authority: the right and the power to act
decisions.reason: The noun means authority given and the power to use it (4:32, 36). Jesus claims the right to do what the scribes said belongs to God alone (5:21).

decisions.choice: on the earth: here and now, among people
decisions.reason: The Son of Man forgives sins now, on earth, not only when God judges.

decisions.choice: the sentence breaks off as Jesus turns to the man
decisions.reason: Jesus begins speaking to the scribes and Pharisees and finishes by speaking to the paralyzed man. Matthew and Mark have the same break (Mark 2:10).

decisions.choice: the Son of Man, with capitals and no gender setting
decisions.reason: A title, as in John 1:51, so it is never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: I will prove to you; the right
alternatives: so that you may know; authority
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jesus is about to do and uses a plain word for authority.

records.source: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀναστὰς ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν, ἄρας ἐφ’ ὃ κατέκειτο, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ δοξάζων τὸν θεόν.
records.gloss: And immediately having stood up before them, having taken up on which he was lying, he went away to the house of him glorifying the God.
pieces: Right away the man stood up in front of them, picked up the bed he had been lying on, and went home giving glory to God.

L.25: And immediately he stood up before them, took up what he had been lying on, and went away to his house, glorifying God.

R.25: The man got up at once while everyone watched. He picked up the mat he had been lying on. Then he went home, giving glory to God.

decisions.choice: glorifying God: praising God for what he had done
decisions.reason: People in Luke give glory to God when they see his work (2:20; 7:16; 13:13; 17:15).

decisions.choice: immediately, and took up what he had been lying on: the healing is complete
decisions.reason: The man who was carried in on the bed now carries the bed.

decisions.choice: giving glory to God
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for glory; Balanced and Readable keep that word.

records.source: καὶ ἔκστασις ἔλαβεν ἅπαντας καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεόν, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν φόβου λέγοντες ὅτι Εἴδομεν παράδοξα σήμερον.
records.gloss: And amazement seized all and they were glorifying the God, and were filled with fear saying that, We have seen extraordinary things today.
pieces: Everyone was overcome with amazement. They glorified God, and full of awe they said, "What we have seen today is beyond belief!"

L.26: And amazement seized [them] all, and they were glorifying God, and they were filled with fear, saying, "We have seen extraordinary things today."

R.26: Everyone was amazed, and they gave glory to God. They were full of fear and wonder. They said, "Today we have seen things we never thought could happen!"

decisions.choice: amazement: astonishment that takes people out of themselves
decisions.reason: The noun can mean a trance (Acts 10:10), but here it is the overwhelming astonishment of the crowd.

decisions.choice: fear: awe before the power of God
decisions.reason: In Luke people are filled with fear when God acts among them (1:65; 7:16).

decisions.choice: extraordinary things: things beyond what anyone expected
decisions.reason: The word means what goes against all expectation.

decisions.choice: awe (B); fear and wonder (R)
decisions.reason: "Fear" alone would suggest terror; the meaning decision explains the sense.

records.source: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἐθεάσατο τελώνην ὀνόματι Λευὶν καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι.
records.gloss: And after these things he went out and saw a tax collector by name Levi sitting at the tax office, and he said to him, Follow me.
pieces: Later, Jesus went out and caught sight of a tax collector named Levi, seated at the place where he collected taxes. Jesus told him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.27: And after these things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.27: Later Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi. Levi was sitting at the table where he collected taxes. Jesus said to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}!"

decisions.choice: a tax collector at his booth: a man collecting tolls and taxes for the ruler
alternatives: a government official in an office
decisions.reason: Tax collectors were despised as cheats and as servants of foreign rulers (3:12). In Galilee they worked for Herod Antipas. Levi sat at a booth where tolls were paid, probably near Capernaum.

decisions.choice: Levi: the man called Matthew in Matthew 9:9
decisions.reason: Matthew's Gospel tells the same call with the name Matthew, and Luke lists a Matthew among the twelve (6:15). Mark calls him Levi son of Alphaeus (Mark 2:14).

decisions.choice: follow me: come with me as my disciple
decisions.reason: The same call as to the fishermen (5:11).

decisions.choice: the place (B) or table (R) where he collected taxes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the place.

records.heading: Levi leaves his tax booth

records.source: καὶ καταλιπὼν πάντα ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: And having left all, having risen up he was following him.
pieces: He stood up, left it all, and began following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.28: And leaving everything, he rose up and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.28: Levi got up, left everything, and followed Jesus.

decisions.choice: he was following: he began to follow and went on following
alternatives: he followed for a short time
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes a following that continued.

decisions.choice: leaving everything: his work and its income
decisions.reason: Levi still has his house (5:29), but he leaves his post as a tax collector. The fishermen did the same (5:11).

decisions.choice: got up, then left everything
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable tell the actions in the order English expects.

records.source: Καὶ ἐποίησεν δοχὴν μεγάλην Λευὶς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἦν ὄχλος πολὺς τελωνῶν καὶ ἄλλων οἳ ἦσαν μετ’ αὐτῶν κατακείμενοι.
records.gloss: And made a feast great Levi for him in the house of him; and there was a crowd great of tax collectors and of others who were with them reclining.
pieces: Levi then gave a large feast at his house in honor of Jesus. A big crowd of tax collectors and other people were guests at the table with them.

L.29: And Levi made a great feast for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in his house, and there was a large crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining [at table] with them.

R.29: Levi gave a big party at his house for Jesus. Many tax collectors and other people were there, eating with Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.

decisions.choice: a feast: a banquet with guests
decisions.reason: The word means a reception for guests (14:13).

decisions.choice: reclining: lying at table, as guests did at a feast
decisions.reason: At formal meals guests lay on couches around a low table, leaning on the left elbow (7:36-38).

decisions.choice: with them: with Jesus and his disciples
decisions.reason: The complaint in 5:30 is addressed to the disciples.

decisions.choice: with Jesus and his disciples
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" are, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: guests at the table
decisions.reason: Balanced says what reclining meant without the unfamiliar custom.

records.heading: Eating with tax collectors and sinners

records.source: καὶ ἐγόγγυζον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίετε καὶ πίνετε;
records.gloss: And were grumbling the Pharisees and the scribes of them toward the disciples of him saying, Why with the tax collectors and sinners do you eat and drink?
pieces: This made the Pharisees and their own scribes grumble. They said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "How can you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"

L.30: And the Pharisees and their scribes were grumbling at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, saying, "Why do you eat and drink with the tax collectors and sinners?"

R.30: The Pharisees and their teachers of the law did not like this. They complained to Jesus's disciples, "You eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners! Why do you do that?"

decisions.choice: grumbling: the word used of Israel grumbling in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament uses this verb for Israel's complaints against Moses and God (Exodus 16:7-8; Numbers 14:27). Luke uses it again when Jesus welcomes sinners (15:2; 19:7).

decisions.choice: sinners: people known for breaking the law or living outside its rules
decisions.reason: The word marked out people whose way of life openly broke the law, and whom careful keepers of the law avoided (7:37, 39; 15:1-2).

decisions.choice: eat and drink with: sharing a table meant accepting people as companions
alternatives: only being in the same room
decisions.reason: To eat with someone was a sign of friendship. The Pharisees were careful about with whom they ate, to keep themselves ritually clean.

decisions.choice: their scribes: scribes who belonged to the Pharisees' party
decisions.reason: Not every scribe was a Pharisee; these were.

decisions.choice: teachers of the law (R); scribes (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in 5:21.

decisions.choice: a statement, then the question
decisions.reason: Readable splits the question into two short sentences.

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ὑγιαίνοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες·
records.gloss: And answering the Jesus said to them, No need have the [ones] being healthy of a physician but the [ones] badly having;
pieces: "People who are well have no use for a doctor," Jesus answered them, "but people who are ill do.

L.31: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Those who are healthy have no need of a physician, but those who are sick [do];

R.31: Jesus answered them, "Healthy people do not need a doctor. Sick people need one.

decisions.choice: the healthy have no need of a doctor: a proverb applied to Jesus's mission
decisions.reason: Jesus answers with a common saying. Like a doctor among the sick, he is among sinners because they are the ones who need him (5:32).

decisions.choice: those having badly: the sick
decisions.reason: "To have badly" is the Greek way of saying someone is ill (7:2).

records.source: οὐκ ἐλήλυθα καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν.
records.gloss: not I have come to call righteous [ones] but sinners to repentance.
pieces: The reason I have come is to call sinners to repentance, not the righteous."

L.32: I have not come to call righteous [people] but sinners to repentance."

R.32: I have not come to call people who are already right with God. I have come to call sinners to turn away from their sins and come back to God."

decisions.choice: the righteous: people who keep the law, or who think they do
alternatives: people who have no sin at all
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the Pharisees in their own terms. Luke shows elsewhere people who trusted that they were righteous and despised others (18:9).

decisions.choice: repentance: turning from sin back to God
decisions.reason: The word John used (3:3, 8). Only Luke has "to repentance" in this saying (compare Mark 2:17).

decisions.choice: call: invite, as to a meal
decisions.reason: The verb is used for inviting guests (14:16-17), which fits the setting at Levi's feast.

decisions.choice: I have come: Jesus speaks of his mission
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the purpose for which he came (19:10).

decisions.choice: people who are already right with God; to turn away from their sins and come back to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains both words.

records.source: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν· Οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου νηστεύουσιν πυκνὰ καὶ δεήσεις ποιοῦνται, ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ τῶν Φαρισαίων, οἱ δὲ σοὶ ἐσθίουσιν καὶ πίνουσιν.
records.gloss: They and said to him, The disciples of John fast often and prayers make, likewise also the [ones] of the Pharisees, the [ones] but yours eat and drink.
pieces: Then they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "John's disciples fast frequently and offer prayers, and the Pharisees' disciples do the same. Yours, though, keep eating and drinking."

L.33: And they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "The disciples of John fast often and make prayers, and likewise also those of the Pharisees, but {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}} eat and drink."

R.33: They said to Jesus, "John's disciples often fast, which means they go without food. They also say prayers. The Pharisees' disciples do the same. But {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples eat and drink!"

decisions.choice: a statement: they said to him, "John's disciples fast", the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: a question: "Why do John's disciples fast ...?", the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts have a statement. Many later ones add "why", making it a question, as in Mark 2:18. The challenge is the same either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: they: the Pharisees and their scribes of 5:30
decisions.reason: Luke goes on with the same conversation at Levi's feast.

decisions.choice: fast: go without food for a time, as part of prayer or mourning
decisions.reason: The law set one day of fasting a year, the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:29). Many devout Jews fasted more; a Pharisee in one of Jesus's stories fasts twice a week (18:12).

decisions.choice: make prayers: pray regularly, perhaps at set times
decisions.reason: John taught his disciples a way to pray (11:1).

decisions.choice: which means they go without food
decisions.reason: Readable explains fasting.

records.heading: Bridegroom, patches and wineskins

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μὴ δύνασθε τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ποιῆσαι νηστεῦσαι;
records.gloss: He and said to them, Not are you able the sons of the bridechamber, in which the bridegroom with them is, to make to fast?
pieces: He answered them, "Would you make the guests at a wedding fast while the bridegroom is still among them?

L.34: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "You are not able to make the sons of the bridal chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them, are you?

R.34: Jesus answered them, "When there is a wedding, the guests do not go without food while the bridegroom is with them. You could not make them do that!

decisions.choice: sons of the bridal chamber: the wedding guests, the bridegroom's friends
decisions.reason: "Sons of" is a Hebrew way of speaking about people who belong to something. These are the friends who celebrate with the bridegroom.

decisions.choice: the question expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The form of the question shows that no one would think of it.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom: a wedding was a time of feasting
decisions.reason: A wedding feast could last a week (Judges 14:12). Fasting belonged to mourning, so to fast at a wedding made no sense.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom: a picture of Jesus, recalling God as Israel's bridegroom
decisions.reason: The prophets picture God rejoicing over his people as a bridegroom over his bride (Isaiah 62:5; Hosea 2:19-20). John the Baptist calls Jesus the bridegroom (John 3:29). Jesus's presence is a time of joy.

decisions.choice: the guests at a wedding
alternatives: the sons of the bridal chamber
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom, lowercase and with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The bridegroom is a figure in a picture, as in John 3:29. Jesus speaks of himself through the picture without naming himself.

records.source: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι, καὶ ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.
records.gloss: Will come but days, and when has been taken away from them the bridegroom, then they will fast in those the days.
pieces: Days are coming, though, when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then, in those days, they will fast."

L.35: But days will come, and when the bridegroom is taken away from them, then they will fast in those days."

R.35: But someday the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then, at that time, they will fast."

decisions.choice: the bridegroom taken away: a first hint of Jesus's death
decisions.reason: A bridegroom is not usually taken away from his own wedding. The words point ahead to Jesus being taken from his disciples (9:22). The verb may echo Isaiah 53:8, where the servant's life is taken away.

decisions.choice: days will come: a way of speaking of the future, often of trouble
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the phrase of coming sorrow (17:22; 21:6; 23:29).

decisions.choice: then they will fast: Jesus's disciples will fast after he is gone
decisions.reason: Jesus does not reject fasting; there is a time for it. The church in Acts fasts and prays (Acts 13:2-3; 14:23).

records.source: ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ἀπὸ ἱματίου καινοῦ σχίσας ἐπιβάλλει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν· εἰ δὲ μήγε, καὶ τὸ καινὸν σχίσει καὶ τῷ παλαιῷ οὐ συμφωνήσει τὸ ἐπίβλημα τὸ ἀπὸ τοῦ καινοῦ.
records.gloss: He was saying and also a parable to them that, No one a piece from a garment new having torn puts on a garment old; if but not, both the new he will tear and to the old will not match the [piece] from the new.
pieces: He told them a parable as well: "Nobody cuts a patch out of a new coat to sew on an old one. If anyone did, the new coat would be ruined, and the patch from the new would not suit the old coat either.

L.36: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also told them a parable: "No one tears a piece from a new garment and puts [it] on an old garment; otherwise, [that person] will both tear the new, and the [piece] from the new will not match the old.

R.36: Jesus also told them a story to explain this. "No one cuts a piece out of new clothes to fix a hole in old clothes. If someone did that, they would ruin the new clothes. And the new piece would not look right on the old clothes.

decisions.choice: parable: a comparison taken from everyday life
decisions.reason: The word covers short sayings and pictures (4:23) as well as stories. Here Jesus gives three pictures (5:36-39).

decisions.choice: otherwise: both garments are spoiled
alternatives: only the old garment is spoiled
decisions.reason: In Luke the loss is double: the new garment is cut up, and the patch does not match the old. Mark's form of the saying speaks of the new patch pulling away from the old (Mark 2:21).

decisions.choice: the new and the old: what Jesus brings cannot be fitted into the old ways
decisions.reason: The pictures answer the question about fasting (5:33). Jesus's new work does not patch up the old customs; trying to join them spoils both.

decisions.choice: garment: the outer cloak
decisions.reason: The word means a cloak worn over the tunic, a valuable piece of clothing.

decisions.choice: coat (B); clothes (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words.

decisions.choice: a story to explain this; to fix a hole
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a parable is here and why someone would cut a patch.

decisions.choice: [that person]
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no stated subject; Literal supplies a general one.

records.source: καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μήγε, ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος ὁ νέος τοὺς ἀσκούς, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐκχυθήσεται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπολοῦνται·
records.gloss: And no one puts wine new into wineskins old; if but not, will burst the wine the new the wineskins, and it will be spilled out and the wineskins will be destroyed;
pieces: Nor does anyone store new wine in old wineskins. That would make the skins split open; the new wine would spill, and the skins would be lost.

L.37: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise, the new wine will burst the wineskins, and it will be spilled out, and the wineskins will be destroyed.

R.37: And no one puts new wine into old bags made of skin. The new wine would make the old skins break open. The wine would pour out, and the skins would be no good anymore.

decisions.choice: new wine in old wineskins: fermenting wine stretches the skin
decisions.reason: Wine was kept in bags made from whole goat skins. New wine was still fermenting and gave off gas. A new skin could stretch; an old one was dry and stiff, and would split.

decisions.choice: bags made of skin
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word.

records.source: ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινοὺς βλητέον.
records.gloss: But wine new into wineskins fresh must be put.
pieces: Instead, new wine has to be put into fresh skins.

L.38: But new wine must be put into fresh wineskins.

R.38: New wine must go into new skins.

decisions.choice: the sentence ends here, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: "and both are kept safe" added, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts end with "must be put". Many later ones add words found in Matthew 9:17. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: new wine, fresh wineskins: two different words for new
decisions.reason: The word used for the wine means recently made; the word used for the skins (and for the garment in 5:36) means not yet used.

decisions.choice: fresh (L, B); new (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the two Greek words apart; Readable uses the plainer word.

records.source: καὶ οὐδεὶς πιὼν παλαιὸν θέλει νέον· λέγει γάρ· Ὁ παλαιὸς χρηστός ἐστιν.
records.gloss: And no one having drunk old desires new; he says for, The old good is.
pieces: And nobody who has been drinking old wine wants the new. 'The old is good,' they say."

L.39: And no one who has drunk old [wine] wants new, for [that person] says, 'The old is good.'"

R.39: And people who have been drinking old wine do not want new wine. They say, 'The old wine is good.'"

decisions.choice: good, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: better, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts have "good"; many later ones have "better". With "good", the drinker is content with the old and does not want to try the new. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the verse belongs to the text, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the verse left out, as in a few early witnesses
decisions.reason: A few witnesses, among them Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts, leave out the verse; the rest have it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: no one who has drunk old wine wants new: people content with the old do not look for the new
alternatives: old wine is better than new
decisions.reason: The saying closes the pictures with a comment on people: many who are used to the old ways will not welcome what Jesus brings.

decisions.choice: [that person] (L); they (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject; the person is anyone who has drunk old wine.
